title: Product Launch: Quality vs Time-to-Market
description: Illustrative example showing how Aura's non-compensatory guarantee prevents masking of critical safety weakness
contextRaw: Should we launch product version A (fast, but incomplete safety testing) or version B (slower, but comprehensive safety validation) or version C (moderate approach)?

criteria.label: Complétude de la validation de sécurité
criteria.description: Étendue des tests de sécurité, conformité réglementaire, durabilité du produit

criteria.label: Coût de développement
criteria.description: Budget requis pour compléter le projet

criteria.label: Capacité de l'équipe

leviersDef.label: Approche de développement

scenarios.label: Lancement Rapide (Option A)
scenarios.description: Commercialisation en 6 mois avec tests de sécurité minimaux
scenarios.auraInsight: Élevé pour délai et coût; DÉFAILLANT pour sécurité (validation: 0). Pondération 3 sur sécurité élimine cette option en logique non-compensatoire.

scenarios.label: Approche Équilibrée (Option B)
scenarios.description: Mise en marché en 10 mois avec validation de sécurité modérée
scenarios.auraInsight: Équilibré: tous les critères à niveau modéré/acceptable. Recommandé par Aura.

scenarios.label: Validation Complète (Option C)
scenarios.description: Déploiement complet avec tests exhaustifs (14 mois)
scenarios.auraInsight: Excellence en sécurité; faible pour délai. Acceptable mais coûteux en temps.

comparisonAnalysis.description: Comparison between Aura non-compensatory and simple weighted-average methods

weighted_average_rankings.note: Weighted average ranks FAST LAUNCH 2nd. The excellent time-to-market (100) and cost efficiency (90) partially compensate for the catastrophic safety failure (0).
Weighted average ranks BALANCED 3rd — lowest overall score because it excels at nothing.
Weighted average ranks COMPREHENSIVE 1st — highest because safety excellence (100) outweighs time/cost penalties.

aura_rankings.reasoning: Aura's non-compensatory guarantee: if safety_validation (with weight 'Essentiel'/3) scores 0, the entire option fails because the min() function in Eq.6 caps the global grade at max(¬ω_i, g_i) = max(0, 0) = 0. No compensating strength in other criteria can override a critical failure.
All criteria meet minimum thresholds under non-compensatory logic. Safety at 50 (Moyen) passes the floor (¬ω=0 < 50). Elected as the safe, defensible choice.

Time-to-market (20) becomes the bottleneck under non-compensatory logic. Safety excellence cannot compensate for delayed market entry when ω_time = 'Important' (2). A rational choice but not the top recommendation.

comparisonAnalysis.key_insight: Divergence: Weighted-average ranks Comprehensive 1st, Balanced 3rd. Aura ranks Balanced 1st, Comprehensive 2nd, and ELIMINATES Fast Launch entirely. The non-compensatory guarantee prevents recommending an option with a critical failure (safety = 0) even when compensating strengths (time-to-market, cost) pull the weighted average upward.
comparisonAnalysis.business_context: In regulated industries (medical, pharma, aerospace), a safety failure is disqualifying—period. No amount of speed or cost savings can justify launching a product that hasn't passed its safety gates. Aura's structure naturally enforces this hard constraint. A weighted-average method requires ad-hoc post-hoc filters ('we'll never score safety at 0 if we didn't validate...'), whereas Aura's architecture makes it structural.
comparisonAnalysis.illustrative_labeling: This example is ILLUSTRATIVE (constructed to highlight method differences) and does NOT reflect real pharmaceutical validation data or timelines. Real examples would use domain-specific impact scales and regulatory thresholds.
